find: RIDDOR requires employers to report certain serious workplace incidents to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE). Reportable incidents include deaths, major injuries (broken bones, amputations, burns requiring hospital treatment), injuries that prevent an employee from working for more than seven consecutive days, work-related diseases, and dangerous occurrences (near misses that could have caused serious harm). Reports must be made without delay, and records kept for at least three years.
replace: RIDDOR requires employers to report specified work-related incidents to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE). Reportable incidents include deaths, specified injuries (such as most fractures and amputations), injuries that prevent an employee from working for more than seven consecutive days, work-related diseases, and specified dangerous occurrences. Deaths, specified injuries and dangerous occurrences must be notified without delay. An over-seven-day injury must be reported within 15 days. Records of reportable cases must be kept for at least three years.
note: F7: Corrects the categories and reporting deadlines.

Indicative content:
• The EHO inspects food businesses for hygiene, storage, equipment, and documentation standards.
• They collect evidence (food samples, photographs, interviews) during inspections.
• They investigate outbreaks of food poisoning to identify the source and prevent further cases.
• They enforce environmental health laws and can prosecute businesses that break the law.
• They award food hygiene ratings (0–5) that are displayed publicly, influencing customer choice.
• Their role protects the public by ensuring food businesses maintain safe standards.
